# Disagreement Log — Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 58

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET (literal) | LOGOS (formal) | PNEUMA (dynamic)
**Total Disagreements:** 9

---

## Disagreement 1 — 58:1 "appointed days" vs. "designated fast days"

- **EMET:** "when you fast on the appointed days"
- **LOGOS:** "when you fast on the appointed days"
- **PNEUMA:** "on the designated fast days"
- **Note:** EMET and LOGOS agree.
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "when you fast on the appointed days" (EMET/LOGOS). The *stationes* (station fasts) are the referent; "appointed" preserves the regulated character.

---

## Disagreement 2 — 58:1 "take no food at all" vs. "do not eat at all"

- **EMET:** "do not eat at all until the ninth hour"
- **LOGOS:** "take no food at all until the ninth hour"
- **PNEUMA:** "eat nothing at all until the ninth hour"
- **Greek:** *mēden geusē* — taste/eat nothing
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "take no food at all until the ninth hour" (LOGOS). "Take no food" is slightly more formal; *geuomai* can mean "taste" but in context means "eat."

---

## Disagreement 3 — 58:1 "save" vs. "whatever is saved"

- **EMET:** "whatever you save from your foods"
- **LOGOS:** "whatever is saved from your foods"
- **PNEUMA:** "whatever you have saved from your normal meals"
- **Greek:** *to perisseuon apo tōn brōmatōn* — the surplus/remainder from the foods
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "whatever is saved from your foods" (LOGOS). The passive "is saved" reflects *perisseuon* as a remainder/surplus rather than active saving. PNEUMA's "normal meals" adds interpretation.

---

## Disagreement 4 — 58:1 "widow or an orphan or to someone in need"

- **EMET:** "give it to a widow or an orphan or to someone in need"
- **LOGOS:** "give it to a widow, or an orphan, or to someone in need"
- **PNEUMA:** "give it to a widow, an orphan, or someone in need"
- **Note:** All three agree on substance.
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "give it to a widow, or an orphan, or to someone in need." The traditional triad of care recipients.

---

## Disagreement 5 — 58:1 "humble yourself" vs. "act of humbling"

- **EMET:** "so you humble yourself...from your humbling"
- **LOGOS:** "so you humble yourself...from your act of humbling"
- **PNEUMA:** "By humbling yourself...by your self-denial"
- **Greek:** *tapeinōsis* — humbling, self-abasement
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "so you humble yourself...from your act of humbling" (LOGOS). The noun *tapeinōsis* is preserved as "act of humbling"; PNEUMA's "self-denial" is too ascetic.

---

## Disagreement 6 — 58:1 "be satisfied" vs. "be filled"

- **EMET:** "the one who receives may be satisfied"
- **LOGOS:** "the one who receives may be filled"
- **PNEUMA:** "will be genuinely satisfied"
- **Greek:** *chortasthē* — to be filled/satisfied/fed to fullness
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "the one who receives may be filled" (LOGOS). *Chortazō* means to fill/feed to satiation; "filled" is more literal; "satisfied" softens the physicality.

---

## Disagreement 7 — 58:2 "will be written down" vs. "will be recorded"

- **EMET:** "this fast will be written down"
- **LOGOS:** "this fast will be recorded"
- **PNEUMA:** "will be counted and recorded"
- **Greek:** *graphēsetai hē nēsteia* — the fast will be written/recorded
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "this fast will be recorded" (LOGOS). "Recorded" is the natural English for heavenly accounting; "written down" (EMET) is slightly redundant.

---

## Disagreement 8 — 58:2 "beautiful and joyful" vs. "beautiful and rejoicing"

- **EMET:** "the service performed in this way is beautiful and joyful"
- **LOGOS:** "the service performed in this way is beautiful and rejoicing"
- **PNEUMA:** "The service you render by doing this is beautiful, joyful"
- **Greek:** *kalos kai hilaros* — beautiful/good and cheerful/joyful/merry
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "the service performed in this way is beautiful and joyful" (EMET/PNEUMA). *Hilaros* = cheerful/joyful; "rejoicing" (LOGOS) makes the adjective into a participle.

---

## Disagreement 9 — 58:3 "observe these things with your children and with all your house"

- **EMET:** "observe these things with your children and with all your house"
- **LOGOS:** "observe these things with your children and with all your household"
- **PNEUMA:** "Observe these things with your children and everyone in your household"
- **Greek:** *meta tōn teknōn sou kai holou tou oikou sou* — with your children and all your house
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "observe these things with your children and with all your household" (LOGOS). "Household" better captures *oikos* as the social unit including slaves, dependents.

---

*End of disagreement log for Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 58.*
